item.title: Yakushima Cedar Forest Trekking — Guide
item.description: Trekking through the ancient cedar forests is the quintessential Yakushima experience, and one of the most profound hikes in Japan. The island’s misty, moss-blanketed primeval forest — said to have inspired the film ‘Princess Mononoke’ — is home to the yakusugi, venerable Japanese cedars over 1,000 years old. The most famous trek leads to Jomon Sugi, the island’s largest and oldest cedar, thought to be thousands of years old — a demanding full-day hike of around 10 hours return, partly along an old forest railway.

item.title: Yakushima Island — Guide
item.description: Yakushima, a mountainous island off the southern coast of Kagoshima, is one of Japan’s most extraordinary natural wonders and a UNESCO World Heritage site. Almost circular and covered in dense, ancient forest rising to peaks nearly 2,000 metres high, it is famous above all for its yakusugi — venerable Japanese cedars over 1,000 years old, some far older. The greatest, Jomon Sugi, is thought to be thousands of years old. The island’s misty, moss-carpeted primeval forests are hauntingly beautiful and are said to have inspired the film ‘Princess Mononoke’.

item.title: Yakushima Whale & Dolphin Watching — Guide
item.description: The warm seas off Yakushima and southern Kagoshima are a rewarding spot for whale and dolphin watching. From roughly January to April, humpback whales migrate through these waters, and boat tours head out for the thrilling chance to see these giant creatures breaching, spouting and diving in the open sea — an unforgettable wildlife spectacle. Pods of dolphins are also frequently encountered year-round, often riding the bow waves of the boats and delighting passengers with their acrobatics.
